A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TAMMs and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The extensive reorganization does not prevent matching the methods and experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original change-description and image-forecasting evaluations, component ablations, qualitative examples, description-length analysis, and training curves.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations of both tasks, ablations, qualitative examples, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: LTAM is renamed Physical Time Encoder (PTE), grouped with CTP under TAM. The temporal-token construction, prompting, composite loss, gated semantic/structural fusion, temporal refinement, and staged training remain substantively the same. The rewritten descriptions do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions train on 37,003 fMoW sequences and evaluate on 150 Google Earth sequences spanning 5–10 years. Temporal change description and future satellite image forecasting remain the evaluated tasks, with no added dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: v1 Table 1 separately compares DeepSeek-VL2 base and supervised-fine-tuned variants. v2 Table 1 retains one DeepSeek-VL2 row with the former base scores and removes the separate fine-tuned row, although its results remain as 'SFT only' in the ablation table. Other comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: v2 Section 4.2.1 describes Qwen2.5-VL-7B and DeepSeek-VL2 as fine-tuned on TAMMs' datasets, replacing v1's explicit base zero-shot/fine-tuned distinction. DeepSeek's retained scores match the earlier base row, so this establishes a reported setting revision without establishing reruns. The rewritten TCS specification also omits explicit normalization and no-change handling.

E4.justification: The same temporal-module and generation-conditioning ablations, qualitative cases, description-length comparison, and training-loss analyses remain. The forecast examples and loss-curve images are identical. The added absolute length-difference column restates the existing comparison rather than introducing a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable statistical uncertainty estimates. Both present point estimates; discussion of future predictive uncertainty does not add uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Between v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 2, ROUGE-L changes from 0.4690 to 0.4678 for 'w/o CTP' and from 0.4678 to 0.4690 for full TAMMs. The main TAMMs scores remain unchanged. v2 also removes the separate main-comparison SFT results, edits displayed DeepSeek descriptions, and adds differences calculated from unchanged average description lengths.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2.3 replaces v1's explicitly normalized centroid distance with a centroid-norm expression without specifying normalization, and omits the special TCS definitions for absent changes. This reduces the completeness of the written mathematical definition without establishing a changed implementation. The method and diffusion-loss equations are otherwise equivalent or relocated; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The joint understanding/forecasting and performance claims remain. v2 adds explicit 'first unified' and 'mutually reinforcing' framing, illustrated as a closed loop in Figure 1, and promotes the existing TCS to a separate 'first metric' contribution. These extend the novelty and interaction claims without adding task coverage or supporting experiments.

C2.justification: v1's detailed limitations section becomes brief future-work discussion in v2 Section 6. Long-horizon, rare-event, efficiency, and uncertainty themes remain, but the explicit greater-than-two-year/error-accumulation qualification and atmospheric/extreme-weather discussion disappear. v2 also develops the argument that global textual guidance is too coarse for fine-grained forecasting control.

D1.justification: The hyperparameter table and hardware are retained. v2 Appendix A.8 clarifies the constant Stage 2 learning rate and removes tentative training language, while the explicit 512×512 resizing instruction and temporal-regularization example disappear. The new reproducibility statement asserts public dataset accessibility but supplies no concrete access route for the curated test set.

R1.justification: The literature discussion is substantially narrowed and repositioned around disjoint understanding/generation paradigms and their unification. The numerical time-series subsection and references including ARIMA, LSTMs, Time-LLM, and several surveys and satellite MLLMs are removed. Video-XL-Pro is added, while the principal evaluated competitors remain cited.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 adds a Task Definition section, moves Related Works after experiments, relocates training formulations and the CTP prompt to appendices, and restructures the appendices with ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-usage statements. Terminology and the author list also change.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a single-column layout, adds a conceptual comparison diagram, revises the framework overview, and redraws the SFCI schematic. The separate task-result tables and ablation tables are merged into two combined tables, and the length table gains a difference column. Existing qualitative examples, distribution plots, and loss curves are relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: The reorganized narrative, consolidated tables, and clearer training prose improve navigation. However, v2 describes MLLM baselines as fine-tuned while retaining the earlier DeepSeek base scores and dropping the separate fine-tuned comparison, weakening experimental traceability. Omitting normalization and no-change handling from the now-prominent TCS definition also reduces reproducibility. These limited substantive losses outweigh the presentation gains.
